title: Unit 2: JavaScript ES6+, DOM Manipulation & Async/Await
subject: Web Development
content:
CHAPTER 1: MODERN JAVASCRIPT ES6+
- let and const: Block-scoped variable declarations.
- Arrow Functions: Concise syntax without own 'this' binding.
- Destructuring: Unpacking values from arrays or objects.
- Spread & Rest Operators (...): Copying arrays/objects or accepting arbitrary arguments.

CHAPTER 2: DOM MANIPULATION
- document.getElementById(), querySelector(), querySelectorAll()
- element.addEventListener('click', handler)
- Creating elements: document.createElement('div')

CHAPTER 3: ASYNCHRONOUS JAVASCRIPT
- JavaScript is single-threaded, using an Event Loop to handle non-blocking asynchronous operations.
- Promises: Object representing the eventual completion (or failure) of an asynchronous operation (Pending, Fulfilled, Rejected).
- Async/Await: Syntactic sugar over Promises providing clean synchronous-looking code structure.

title: Unit 3: Database Normalization & SQL Complete Notes
subject: DBMS
content:
CHAPTER 1: DATABASE NORMALIZATION OVERVIEW
Normalization is the systematic process of organizing data in a database to reduce redundancy and avoid insertion, update, and deletion anomalies.

CHAPTER 2: NORMAL FORMS EXPLAINED
1. First Normal Form (1NF):
   - Each table cell contains a single value (atomic values).
   - Each record needs to be unique.

2. Second Normal Form (2NF):
   - Must be in 1NF.
   - No Partial Dependency: All non-key attributes must be fully functionally dependent on the primary key.

3. Third Normal Form (3NF):
   - Must be in 2NF.
   - No Transitive Dependency: Non-key attributes must not depend on other non-key attributes.

4. Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF):
   - Stricter form of 3NF where for every functional dependency X -> Y, X must be a super key.

title: Unit 4: Binary Trees, BST & Graph Algorithms
subject: Data Structures
content:
CHAPTER 1: BINARY SEARCH TREES (BST)
Properties:
- Left subtree values < Root value.
- Right subtree values > Root value.
- Both left and right subtrees must also be BSTs.

Traversals:
- In-Order (Left, Root, Right): Returns nodes in ascending sorted order.
- Pre-Order (Root, Left, Right): Useful for tree cloning.
- Post-Order (Left, Right, Root): Useful for tree deletion.

Time Complexity:
- Average: O(log n) for Search, Insert, and Delete.
- Worst Case (Skewed): O(n).

CHAPTER 2: GRAPH TRAVERSALS
- Breadth-First Search (BFS): Uses Queue data structure, explores neighbor nodes level by level.
- Depth-First Search (DFS): Uses Stack (or recursion), explores as deep as possible before backtracking.

title: Unit 5: CPU Scheduling, Deadlocks & Memory Management
subject: Operating Systems
content:
CHAPTER 1: CPU SCHEDULING ALGORITHMS
- First-Come, First-Served (FCFS): Non-preemptive, simple, suffers from Convoy Effect.
- Shortest Job First (SJF): Gives minimum average waiting time. Preemptive variant: SRTF.
- Round Robin (RR): Preemptive, utilizes time quantum (TQ), fair for time-sharing systems.

CHAPTER 2: DEADLOCK PRINCIPLES
Four Necessary Coffman Conditions for Deadlock:
1. Mutual Exclusion
2. Hold and Wait
3. No Preemption
4. Circular Wait

Deadlock Handling:
- Deadlock Prevention
- Deadlock Avoidance (Banker's Algorithm)
- Deadlock Detection and Recovery
